title: Bubble Sort: the biggest value bubbles to the end

Match each bubble sort idea to its meaning

goal: After this you can sort an array with Bubble Sort, explain what happens in each pass, say why the inner loop shrinks, and trace a pass by hand on four or five numbers.
warmup: Imagine five students standing in a line for assembly, and the teacher says: stand in order of height, shortest first. You cannot see the whole line at once, so you only look at the two students next to each other. If the left one is taller, they swap places. You walk down the line doing this for every pair. At the end of the walk the tallest student has been pushed all the way to the right end, like a bubble floating up in a glass of water. Then you repeat the walk, but the last student is already correct, so you stop one place earlier each time.
definition: Bubble Sort is a simple way to sort an array. It repeatedly compares two NEIGHBOURING elements and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. One full trip along the array is called a pass. After pass 1 the largest value has bubbled to the last position. After pass 2 the second largest is in the second-to-last position, and so on. An array of N elements needs at most N - 1 passes. Sorting ascending means smallest first. Sorting descending means largest first.
howItWorks: Use the Visualize tab and press Play. Look at the bars. The two bars being compared are highlighted. If the left bar is taller, they swap. Here is the logic in four lines. (1) Outer loop: pass = 0 to N - 2. That is N - 1 passes. (2) Inner loop: j = 0 while j < N - 1 - pass. In each step compare a[j] with a[j + 1]. (3) If a[j] > a[j + 1] swap them using a temporary variable. (4) After the inner loop, the biggest unsorted value is in its final place. Why does the inner loop shrink? After pass 0 the last 1 value is final. After pass 1 the last 2 values are final. So pass number 'pass' needs to look only at the first N - pass values, which means the last pair to compare is (N - 2 - pass, N - 1 - pass), and that is why the condition is j < N - 1 - pass. Counting comparisons: pass 0 makes N - 1, pass 1 makes N - 2, ... the last pass makes 1. The total is (N - 1) + (N - 2) + ... + 1 = N(N - 1) / 2. For N = 5 that is 10. Optional improvement: use a bool flag called swapped. Set it to false at the start of each pass and to true when a swap happens. If a whole pass finishes with swapped still false, the array is already sorted and we can break. For descending order, change only the comparison: use a[j] < a[j + 1].

The unsorted data. The same array will be rearranged in place.
Outer loop: one round per pass. N - 1 passes are enough.
Inner loop: walks along the unsorted part. N - 1 - pass means it gets shorter every pass, because the last values are already in place.

Swap step 2: move the right value to the left.

A small loop that prints all elements of the array.
After all passes, the whole array is in ascending order.

sample.title: Trace one Bubble Sort pass

explanation.text: Start: 7 3 5 1.
Only one pass, so only the inner loop. j goes 0, 1, 2 (three pairs).
Pair 1 is (7, 3), pair 2 is (7, 5), pair 3 is (7, 1).
The big value 7 is always on the left, so every comparison asks for a swap.
Counts the swaps. Here 3 comparisons gave 3 swaps.
The result is 3 5 1 7. The largest value 7 is in its final place; the other values are only partly sorted.

steps.note: The array holds 7, 3, 5, 1 at positions 0 to 3.
We count how many comparisons we make.
We count how many swaps we make.
7 > 3 is true, so swap them. The 7 moved one step to the right.
7 > 5 is true, so swap. The 7 keeps bubbling to the right.
7 > 1 is true, so swap. The largest value 7 is now at the end. The loop stops because j would be 3.
Pass 1 is complete. Print the label.
Prints the array: 7 has bubbled to the last place.

variations.when: Data may already be sorted; saves passes
Standard, does not re-check the sorted end
variations.example: for (int j = 0; j < N - 1 - pass; j++)

variations.when: Always, to avoid losing a value

mistakes.error: No compiler error. Without a temporary box the values are copied, not swapped. For {5, 1, 4, 2, 8} the program prints 1 1 2 2 8: the data is destroyed.

mistakes.wrong:
for (int j = 0; j < N; j++) {
    if (a[j] > a[j + 1]) { ... }   // reads a[N]
mistakes.right: for (int j = 0; j < N - 1 - pass; j++)
mistakes.error: Usually no compiler error. When j = N - 1 the program reads a[N], which is outside the array (undefined behaviour). It may print garbage or give a wrong order.

mistakes.right: Wrap the inner loop in: for (int pass = 0; pass < N - 1; pass++)
mistakes.error: No compiler error. One pass only moves the largest value to the end. For {5, 1, 4, 2, 8} the output is 1 4 2 5 8, which is not sorted.
No compiler error. The wrong comparison sorts in descending order: 8 5 4 2 1.

examTips: Learn the 3 lines of a swap by heart: temp = a[j]; a[j] = a[j + 1]; a[j + 1] = temp;
After pass 1 the largest value is at the end. After pass 2 the second largest is next to it. Say this in a trace question.
N values need N - 1 passes. The inner loop limit is N - 1 - pass. Comparisons in total: N(N - 1) / 2.
Ascending uses a[j] > a[j + 1]. Descending uses a[j] < a[j + 1]. Only this sign changes.
When asked to trace, write one row per pass: the comparisons, which pairs swapped, and the array after the pass.
romanSummary: Bubble Sort mein hum do paas wali values compare karte hain aur galat order mein hon to swap kar dete hain.
Har pass ke baad sab se bari value bubble ban kar aakhir mein pohanch jati hai.
N values ke liye N - 1 passes chahiye hote hain aur inner loop j < N - 1 - pass tak chalta hai.
Swap ke liye temp variable zaroori hai: temp = a[j]; a[j] = a[j + 1]; a[j + 1] = temp;
Ascending ke liye a[j] > a[j + 1] aur descending ke liye a[j] < a[j + 1] likho. Agar kisi pass mein swap na ho to array sorted hai.

practice.prompt: After the FIRST pass of Bubble Sort (ascending), where is the largest value?
practice.hint: The big value bubbles to the end.
practice.explanation: In pass 1 the largest value is carried to the right by every swap until it reaches the last place.

practice.prompt: How many passes are enough to sort 6 numbers with Bubble Sort?
practice.explanation: Each pass fixes the largest remaining value. After 5 passes the last value is automatically correct.
4 is compared with 3, 2 and 1 and swapped every time. The others keep their order: 3 2 1 4.
Pass 1 makes 2 swaps and pass 2 makes 1 swap, so 3 swaps in total.

practice.hint: Save one value before it is overwritten.
practice.explanation: The first line destroys the old a[j]. A temporary variable keeps it safe, so the second value can be copied back.

practice.hint: After each pass one more value is final at the right end.
practice.explanation: In pass number 'pass' the last 'pass' values are already in place, and a[j + 1] must stay inside the array, so j < N - 1 - pass.

practice.prompt: Write the loops that sort the array a[N] in DESCENDING order with Bubble Sort (N and a are already declared).
practice.hint: Only one sign changes compared to ascending.
practice.explanation: With a[j] < a[j + 1] the smaller value is pushed to the right, so each pass moves the smallest remaining value to the end and the array ends largest first.

practice.prompt: How many comparisons does Bubble Sort (no early exit) make on 6 values?

quiz.prompt: What does Bubble Sort compare in each step?
options: The first and last element only
The smallest element with every other element
quiz.hint: Think of the students in the line.
quiz.explanation: It compares a[j] with a[j + 1] and swaps them if they are in the wrong order.

quiz.prompt: After each pass, which value is in its final place?
quiz.hint: It bubbles to the right end.
quiz.explanation: Each pass carries the largest remaining value to the end of the unsorted part.

quiz.prompt: Why is the inner loop limit N - 1 - pass?
options: The last values are already sorted, and a[j + 1] must stay inside the array
To make the program faster to type
quiz.answer: The last values are already sorted, and a[j + 1] must stay inside the array
quiz.hint: What is already correct after pass 1?
quiz.explanation: Each pass fixes one more value at the end, so the inner loop can stop one step earlier.

quiz.prompt: Which change sorts in descending order?
options: Use a[j] < a[j + 1] in the if
quiz.answer: Use a[j] < a[j + 1] in the if
quiz.explanation: With < the larger value moves left and the smaller one moves right.

quiz.prompt: What does the swapped flag help with?
options: Stopping early when a pass makes no swap
quiz.answer: Stopping early when a pass makes no swap
quiz.hint: What does no swap in a whole pass tell you?
quiz.explanation: If no pair was swapped, every neighbour pair is in order, so the array is sorted and the loop can break.
